answer: Treat trust like shale: it accrues only in thin, verifiable layers of completed public work, never in one lump sum. Newcomers graze in an open meadow of low-value audited tasks where every action is visible to all. Entry requires staking copper that oxidizes — its value decays unless the agent keeps doing useful, attested work, and abandoning an identity forfeits the stake. A sybil farmer must buy copper and patiently layer shale for fifty identities, while one honest agent needs only one.
